title: Preview stream orchestration
note: Wave 2 verifies the neutral stream manager and readiness gate against deterministic simulated sources and a scripted evidence provider. Every test is offline. Nothing is run against hardware, RTSP, a decoder or any Seestar code. Stream orchestration, readiness gating and recovery rules are local DB-03 semantics (docs/DB-03_PREVIEW_MANAGER.md), not contract requirements.

evidence_classes.offline: Deterministic tests against simulated sources and scripted evidence.
evidence_classes.hardware: None. Wave 2 makes no hardware claim; hardware validation is Wave 5.

not_claimed.REQ-058: Concerns Telemetry samples only (decision D3). Image freshness is a separate local definition.
not_claimed.REQ-057: Fresh-evidence enforcement for safety-sensitive Commands belongs to DB-04. The readiness gate is a preview-open precondition, not a Command safety predicate.
not_claimed.hardware: No hardware evidence of any kind is claimed.

local_semantics.text: At most two active streams, at most one active stream per camera; duplicate and over-limit opens are refused without side effects.
Cameras are isolated: loss, open failure, unexpected poll exception, gate denial or close failure of one never stops the other.
A stream opens only on an explicit open_stream call that passes the gate; nothing opens on its own.

The gate allows only fresh AVAILABLE evidence attributed to the same provider, Connection, device and camera; UNKNOWN, UNAVAILABLE, stale, missing, mismatched, future-dated or failing evidence denies.
A denied gate never builds or opens a source: factory calls and source open() calls are zero.
Connection state is a necessary precondition, never sufficient; the gate has no Connection-state input and reads evidence anew on every open.

A LOST stream is never reactivated; recovery builds a new stream with a new identity after new positive evidence strictly newer than the end of the previous stream. Network recovery implies nothing about camera readiness.
close_all and a disconnected Connection close every stream, release each source exactly once, and block further opens; operations are idempotent.

Old images are never presented as fresh: view re-runs liveness; a failed clock, failed liveness check, backward clock, repeated uncorroborated content or lost stream can only yield fresh=False, and fresh_pixels then returns nothing.
Exceptions during open, poll and close are contained, reported as fixed category tokens and carry no device data.
The manager and gate expose no command surface and no startup, shutdown or arming of cameras.

REQ-016.text: Preview half: the manager exposes read-only runtime image evidence and freshness-confirmed views.

REQ-018.text: Manager outputs are runtime evidence and in-memory pixels; a full simulated manager exercise leaves a canonical database and its directory untouched and no output carries a domain identity.

REQ-022.text: Opening, polling and closing preview streams submit no Commands: no command surface exists and a denied gate has no side effects.

REQ-030.text: Evidence from simulated sources stays marked simulated through the manager.

REQ-031.text: Manager scenarios with simulated sources are deterministic.

REQ-059.text: Reading preview evidence and images alters no device state; readiness evidence is read-only and a denial opens nothing.

REQ-063.text: Simulator preview scenarios drive the same manager, gate and stream concepts a physical provider will use.

REQ-032.text: No canonical domain identity is created or replaced.

REQ-033.text: Preview evidence never becomes a Capture or Frame.

REQ-052.text: The manager imports no vendor, domain or storage code.

REQ-064.text: A stream, view or readiness decision proves no Session, Observation, Capture or Frame exists.

REQ-067.text: No Acquisition Execution surface in the manager.
